children: GOLDMAN SEES PRIVATE CREDIT REBOUND, WARNS OF SOFTWARE STRAIN

Global private credit fundraising rebounded in the second quarter, Goldman Sachs said, suggesting investor concerns over retail fund redemptions are yet to spill over into the institutional market that still dominates the asset class.

The rebound matters for direct lenders, business development companies and private equity-backed borrowers because institutional funds account for more than 85% of private credit assets under management and have more limited redemption risks than retail-focused vehicles.

Through August 25, global private credit fundraising totalled $33 billion in the third quarter, putting the period on track to meet or exceed the $45 billion raised a year earlier, Goldman Sachs analysts led by Amanda Lynam said.

The Wall Street brokerage attributed the improvement in sentiment partly to investors becoming more familiar with differences between retail and institutional structures, reducing the scope for "extrapolating" retail redemption dynamics to the broader market.
Recent redemption spikes at retail-focused vehicles include Blackstone's BCRED and alternative asset manager Blue Owl.

Goldman believes software has become the sector's key area to focus on, for both fundamental credit risks and potential source of deal opportunities. The sector is private credit's largest industry exposure and could face "additional valuation pressure and disruption" among some legacy businesses from AI-related risks.
